topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer treatment approaches and their modes of action.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review traditional cancer treatment modalities, detailing the principles and limitations of surgical resection, radiotherapy, and the mechanisms, successes, and systemic toxicities of cytotoxic chemotherapeutics.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic biological vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies that exploit tumor-specific vulnerabilities, such as hormone receptor reliance, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, oncolytic viral susceptibility, and synthetic lethality from DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors, resistance mechanisms, and drug addiction
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss targeted molecular therapies designed against oncogenic driver kinases alongside the clinical challenges of target mutations, bypass signaling, and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapeutic approaches utilizing engineered monoclonal antibodies to block receptor signaling, recruit immune effector mechanisms, or deliver targeted cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunology, immune checkpoint blockade, and engineered T-cell therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the interaction between the immune system and tumors, covering evidence for immunosurveillance, checkpoint inhibition, neoantigen recognition, bispecific engagers, and CAR T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Systemic challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broader landscape of oncology, assessing historical survival trends, persistent clinical challenges like heterogeneity and trial design, and ethical dilemmas surrounding future therapies.
